text:
dana: FYI ran the int8 bring-up for firefly-embed-1b (baseline float16 -> int8 symmetric per-tensor) against the standard holdout. recall@10 dropped 0.92 -> 0.86, silhouette also down ~0.07. filing here before I dig deeper.
ricardo: ugh. did you use per-channel or per-tensor quant? that delta smells like coarse quantization.
anya: can you paste the command and the eval summary? also which dataset/seed?
dana: command below. dataset is semantic-holdout-v3, seed 42.
```
./run_eval --model firefly-embed-1b --quantize int8 --quant-mode symmetric --dataset semantic-holdout-v3 --seed 42 --batch 256
```

```
Summary: recall@1 0.73 -> 0.70
recall@5 0.86 -> 0.82
recall@10 0.92 -> 0.86
silhouette 0.34 -> 0.27
mean_cosine_shift 0.018
```
samir: did you normalize embeddings before computing recall? we usually L2-normalize for cosine.
dana: yes normalized both baseline and quant. verified embedding dims match.
anya: link to the UMAP and clustering dashboard? we should check if topk neighbors changed vs drift in distribution.
dana: dashboard: https://redwood-internal/embeds/firefly-1b/int8/holdout-v3
eval-bot: Job 47832 completed: full-holdout sweep (int8) — artifacts uploaded to the dashboard.
ricardo: quick guess — layernorm folding or fused ops changed dynamic range and per-tensor symmetric quant can't capture head-wise variations. try per-channel quant and per-channel zero-point.
dana: re-ran with per-channel quant (per-channel asymmetric) and recall@10 improved to 0.90, silhouette 0.31. still below float16 but much better.
anya: nice. can you run an int8 per-channel with activation clipping (0.995 percentile) and also try out per-channel quant but with per-channel-absmax scaling? sometimes that helps on LN-heavy models.
dana: scheduling those now. also toggling KV-cache usage had no effect in the small test.
samir: another quick check — compare cosine similarity histogram for matched pairs (baseline vs quant). if there's a bimodal shift we might have a particular layer collapse.
dana: attached a small table in the dashboard. mean cosine of positive pairs: 0.88 -> 0.85, but std increased from 0.03 -> 0.07.
ops-bot: FYI reduced batch size on inference nodes due to memory pressure during large-batch quant runs, might affect microbatch stats.
ricardo: action list: 1) dana finish per-channel + clipping runs and upload eval artifacts (assigned dana). 2) samir run layerwise cosine diff to spot offending layers (assigned samir). 3) anya run a focused kNN stability test (k=1..20) across cohorts (assigned anya). 4) if per-channel+clipping still bad, pin float16 for canary and notify platform.
dana: acked. will drop results here in ~2 hours.
anya: also let's add a small AB on prod-like traffic (sampled) to check latency and recall tradeoffs before making rollout decision.
samir: one more note — when you rerun, include a quick smoke with quantize-only-weights vs quantize-weights+activations. sometimes quantizing activations kills short queries.
dana: good call, will include that. :thumbsup:
ricardo: thanks — this looks like progress. documenting thread for postmortem if needed. :memo:
